speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin, are you experiencing any neck pain or stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) causing Pancoast syndrome.

The significant weight loss, chronic smoking history, and specific pattern of right arm weakness and sensory loss strongly suggest a lung apex tumor compressing the brachial plexus. Can you confirm if the weakness is specifically affecting the muscles at the base of your thumb and index finger?
